title: Computer Fundamentals
summary: Generations of computers, types, basic organisation (CPU, ALU, CU), pioneers and the abbreviations bank. Two to three guaranteed marks in the Tier-2 Computer Knowledge Test and the base for every other computer topic.

subtopics.title: Five generations of computers
subtopics.concept:
Computers are classified into five generations by the switching technology used.

| Generation | Period | Technology | Examples | Character |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1st | 1940-56 | Vacuum tubes | ENIAC, UNIVAC-I, EDVAC | Room-sized, huge heat, machine language |
| 2nd | 1956-63 | Transistors | IBM 1401, IBM 7094 | Smaller, faster, more reliable |
| 3rd | 1964-71 | Integrated Circuits (IC) | IBM 360, PDP-8 | Keyboard/monitor input, OS appeared |
| 4th | 1971-present | Microprocessor (VLSI/ULSI) | Intel 4004, PCs, laptops | CPU on a single chip; personal computing |
| 5th | present & beyond | AI, parallel & quantum processing | Robotics, expert systems | Natural-language and learning machines |

Key firsts: **ENIAC** (Electronic Numerical Integrator And Computer, 1946) was the first general-purpose electronic digital computer, built by J. P. Eckert and John Mauchly. **UNIVAC-I** (1951) was the first commercially available computer. **Intel 4004** (1971) was the first microprocessor. The stored-program (von Neumann) architecture was proposed by John von Neumann for EDVAC.

tricks.title: Generation ladder mnemonic
tricks.body: **V**acuum tube -> **T**ransistor -> **I**C -> **M**icroprocessor -> **A**I = "**V**ery **T**iny **I**Cs **M**ade **A**I". Five words = five generations, in order.

tricks.title: Firsts trio
tricks.body: **ENIAC 1946** = first electronic general-purpose computer; **UNIVAC-I 1951** = first *commercial* one; **Intel 4004 1971** = first *microprocessor*. Remember 1946 -> 1951 -> 1971 as "built, sold, shrunk".

example.solution: UNIVAC-I (1951), by Eckert-Mauchly. ENIAC was never sold.

mistakes: Choosing 'transistor' for the 3rd generation - transistors are 2nd generation; ICs are 3rd.
Calling UNIVAC the first computer - it was the first *commercial* computer; ENIAC came first.
Marking microprocessor as 3rd generation - microprocessors (Intel 4004) define the 4th.

subtopics.title: Types of computers
subtopics.concept:
By size and power:

| Type | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Supercomputer | Scientific simulation, weather, defence | PARAM series (C-DAC, India), Frontier (USA) |
| Mainframe | Bulk transaction processing - banks, railways, census | IBM zSeries |
| Minicomputer | Mid-size firms, multi-user departments | PDP-11 |
| Microcomputer / Personal computer | One user: desktop, laptop, tablet | PCs |
| Workstation | High-end single-user technical work (CAD, design) | Sun/HP workstations |
| Embedded computer | Inside one appliance - washing machine, car ECU, IoT | Microcontrollers |

India's first indigenous supercomputer was **PARAM 8000** (1991), built by **C-DAC** under Vijay Bhatkar. Weather supercomputers **Pratyush** and **Mihir** serve the India Meteorological Department.

By working principle: **Analog** (measures continuous quantities, e.g. speedometer-type devices), **Digital** (counts with 0/1, general purpose), **Hybrid** (both - ICU monitors, petrol pumps).

tricks.title: Size ladder
tricks.body: "**S**ome **M**inisters **M**ust **P**romise **S**peed" - Supercomputer > Mainframe > Minicomputer > PC (Micro) > Smartphone/embedded, largest to smallest.

example.q: A bank's central transaction server is which class?
example.solution: Mainframe - designed for massive, reliable bulk transactions.

tricks.title: PARAM pin
tricks.body: PARAM = India's supercomputer series, built by **C-DAC, Pune**; PARAM 8000 came in **1991**. Pair it with 'Vijay Bhatkar = father of Indian supercomputing'.

example.solution: C-DAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing), 1991.

mistakes: Calling a mainframe a supercomputer - mainframes optimise many simultaneous transactions, supercomputers optimise raw calculation speed.
Attributing PARAM to ISRO or BARC - it is a C-DAC product.
Hybrid computers are not 'half hardware-software'; they combine analog measurement with digital processing.

subtopics.title: Basic organisation: CPU, memory, I/O
subtopics.concept:
A computer follows the **von Neumann (stored-program) architecture**: instructions and data live in the same memory, and the machine repeatedly fetches and executes them.

**Block diagram:** Input devices -> **CPU** <-> **Memory** -> Output devices, with the system bus (data bus, address bus, control bus) carrying signals on the motherboard.

**CPU (Central Processing Unit)** - the 'brain' - has three parts:

| Part | Job |
|---|---|
| ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) | Arithmetic (+, -, x, /) and logic (compare, AND/OR) operations |
| CU (Control Unit) | Directs traffic: fetches, decodes, coordinates all units; does NOT process data itself |
| Registers | Fastest, tiny storage inside CPU (accumulator, program counter, instruction register) |

**Machine cycle** for one instruction: **Fetch -> Decode -> Execute -> Store**. CPU speed is measured in GHz (billions of clock cycles per second). Other board parts: chipset, expansion slots, CMOS battery, ports. **BIOS/UEFI** firmware wakes the hardware at power-on (see software-os topic).

tricks.title: FDES chant
tricks.body: "**F**at **D**ogs **E**at **S**nacks" = Fetch, Decode, Execute, Store - the machine cycle order. Every instruction, every time.

tricks.title: ALU vs CU
tricks.body: **ALU = Actual Labour Unit** (does the sums); **CU = traffic Constable, Untouched by maths** (only directs). If a question says 'performs calculations' -> ALU; 'coordinates/controls' -> CU.

mistakes: Saying the CU performs arithmetic - it only controls; arithmetic belongs to the ALU.
Reversing Execute and Decode in the machine cycle.
Thinking registers are slower than RAM - registers are the fastest storage in the whole machine.

subtopics.title: Pioneers and programming-language levels
subtopics.concept:
| Person | Known as |
|---|---|
| Charles Babbage | Father of the computer (designed the Analytical Engine, 1837) |
| Ada Lovelace | First programmer (notes on the Analytical Engine) |
| Alan Turing | Father of theoretical computer science & AI (Turing machine, Turing test) |
| John von Neumann | Stored-program architecture |
| Tim Berners-Lee | Inventor of the WWW |
| Grace Hopper | COBOL pioneer, coined 'debugging' (moth in Mark II) |
| Blaise Pascal | Early mechanical adder (Pascaline) |
| Gottfried Leibniz | Stepped reckoner (multiply/divide) |

**Language levels:**

| Level | Form | Translated by | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1GL Machine | 0s and 1s | Needs no translator | CPU instructions |
| 2GL Assembly | Mnemonics (ADD, MOV) | Assembler | 8086 assembly |
| 3GL High-level | English-like | Compiler or interpreter | FORTRAN (1957, first major HLL), COBOL (1959), C, Java, Python |
| 4GL | Declarative, close to results | Built into DBMS/tools | SQL, report generators |
| 5GL | Constraint/AI based | Inference engines | Prolog, Lisp (used in AI) |

**Compiler** converts the whole program to object code in one pass before running (C, C++). **Interpreter** translates and runs line by line (classic Python, JavaScript). **Assembler** converts assembly mnemonics to machine code. HTML is a *markup* language, not a programming language.

tricks.title: Compiler vs Interpreter
tricks.body: **C**ompiler = **C**omplete (whole program first, fast execution, shows all errors together); **I**nterpreter = **I**nstant (line by line, stops at first error). C/C++ -> compiler; Python/JS -> interpreter.

example.q: A language translated line by line, stopping at the first error, uses?

mistakes: Calling HTML a programming language - it only structures/markups content.
Saying machine language needs an assembler - assembly (2GL) does; 1GL needs no translation.
Mixing Ada Lovelace (first programmer) with Grace Hopper (COBOL pioneer).

subtopics.title: Core abbreviations and full forms
subtopics.concept:
High-frequency full forms (learn as a table, SSC asks these directly):

| Short | Full form |
|---|---|
| CPU / ALU / CU | Central Processing Unit / Arithmetic Logic Unit / Control Unit |
| RAM / ROM | Random Access Memory / Read Only Memory |
| PROM / EPROM / EEPROM | Programmable / Erasable Programmable / Electrically Erasable Programmable ROM |
| VDU | Visual Display Unit (monitor) |
| USB | Universal Serial Bus |
| LCD / LED / OLED | Liquid Crystal Display / Light Emitting Diode / Organic LED |
| UPS | Uninterruptible Power Supply |
| BIOS | Basic Input Output System |
| POST | Power-On Self-Test |
| GUI / CLI | Graphical / Command Line Interface |
| OCR / OMR / MICR | Optical Character Recognition / Optical Mark Recognition / Magnetic Ink Character Recognition |
| DPI | Dots Per Inch (printer resolution) |
| AI | Artificial Intelligence |
| PCB | Printed Circuit Board |
| PDA | Personal Digital Assistant |
| CRT | Cathode Ray Tube (old bulky monitor) |
| HDD / SSD | Hard Disk Drive / Solid State Drive |
| CAD | Computer-Aided Design |
| IC / VLSI | Integrated Circuit / Very Large Scale Integration |

Abbreviations for internet/networking (HTTP, URL, ISP...) are collected in the internet-email and networking topics.

tricks.title: ROM family ladder
tricks.body: P -> EP -> EEPROM: each generation gets *easier* to erase - PROM (once, at manufacture/programming), EPROM (erase with **UV light**), EEPROM (erase **electrically**, in circuit). "UV for EPROM, Electricity for EEPROM."

tricks.title: OCR-OMR-MICR trio
tricks.body: OCR reads **Characters** (printed text -> editable text), OMR reads **Marks** (exam bubbles), MICR reads **Ink** on **cheques** (banks). Characters, Marks, Ink = CRM.

mistakes: Expanding UPS as 'Uninterrupted' - the accepted form is **Uninterruptible** Power Supply.
Reading POST as 'Power On System Test' - it is **Power-On Self-Test**.
Confusing DPI (dots per inch, printers) with PPI (pixels per inch, screens).

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Which generation used transistors/ICs/vacuum tubes?' or a statement asking the generation of ENIAC/IBM 1401.
pyqPatterns.approach: Recall the ladder Vacuum tube -> Transistor -> IC -> Microprocessor -> AI and match the technology or the named machine.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'What is the full form of BIOS/ALU/MICR?' - plain expansion questions.
pyqPatterns.approach: Use the abbreviation table; eliminate options that expand the letters plausibly but wrongly (e.g. 'Uninterrupted' for UPS).
Keep the trio ENIAC 1946 (first electronic), UNIVAC-I 1951 (first commercial), Intel 4004 1971 (first microprocessor) plus Babbage/Ada/Turing pinned.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Which unit performs arithmetic?', 'correct order of fetch/decode/execute/store'.
pyqPatterns.approach: ALU calculates, CU controls; cycle is always Fetch -> Decode -> Execute -> Store.

pyqPatterns.howToSpot: 'Which is not system software / not an operating system / which is a markup language?'.
pyqPatterns.approach: Classify each option into OS / utility / application / markup before answering.

solvedExamples.q:
Arrange the computer generations in order of their defining technology:
A. Integrated Circuits  B. Vacuum Tubes  C. Microprocessor  D. Transistors
solvedExamples.solution: Generation order: 1st vacuum tubes (B) -> 2nd transistors (D) -> 3rd ICs (A) -> 4th microprocessor (C). So the sequence B-D-A-C is correct.
solvedExamples.shortcut: Ladder mnemonic "Very Tiny ICs Made AI" - just map the four options onto the ladder; no dates needed.

solvedExamples.q:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?
1. ENIAC was the first general-purpose electronic digital computer.
2. UNIVAC-I was the first computer to use vacuum tubes.
solvedExamples.solution: Statement 1 is correct - ENIAC (1946) was the first general-purpose electronic digital computer. Statement 2 is wrong: UNIVAC-I (1951) was the first *commercial* computer, and vacuum tubes were the 1st-generation technology used already by ENIAC.
solvedExamples.shortcut: If a statement pairs UNIVAC with 'first', check the exact phrase: 'first commercial' is right, almost anything else ('first computer', 'first vacuum-tube computer') is the trap.

solvedExamples.q: Which CPU unit coordinates and controls all parts of the computer but does not itself perform calculations?
solvedExamples.solution: The Control Unit directs the flow of data and instructions and coordinates all units; actual arithmetic/logic is done by the ALU. Registers are tiny storage locations, and memory only holds data.
solvedExamples.shortcut: 'Coordinates/controls/directs' -> CU; 'calculates/compares' -> ALU. The verbs in the question are the answer.

solvedExamples.q: In a language translated line by line with execution stopping at the first erroneous line, the translator is a:
solvedExamples.solution: An interpreter converts and executes high-level code one line at a time and halts at the first error. A compiler translates the entire program before execution (reporting all errors together), an assembler handles assembly language, and a linker joins compiled modules.
solvedExamples.shortcut: "Line by line" in the question points straight to interpreter; "whole program at once" would mean compiler.

practice.q: Transistors were used as the basic technology of which generation of computers?
practice.solution: The 2nd generation (1956-63) replaced vacuum tubes with transistors, making computers smaller, faster and more reliable. 1st = vacuum tubes, 3rd = ICs, 4th = microprocessors.
practice.shortcut: Generation ladder: Vacuum -> Transistor -> IC -> Microprocessor -> AI. Transistor is the 2nd rung.

options: Electronic Number Integrating and Computing Engine
Electronic Numerical Index Analyser and Computer
practice.solution: ENIAC = Electronic Numerical Integrator And Computer, built by Eckert and Mauchly at the University of Pennsylvania.
practice.shortcut: Trap options all start with 'Electronic/Electrical'; remember the key words 'Numerical Integrator And Computer'.

practice.q: Which of the following is regarded as the first commercially available computer?
practice.solution: UNIVAC-I (1951) was the first computer produced and sold commercially. ENIAC was a one-off military project; EDVAC was a stored-program research machine; IBM 360 is a 3rd-generation family (1964).
practice.shortcut: UNIVAC = the first computer you could BUY; ENIAC = the first one ever BUILT electronically.

practice.q: The Intel 4004, released in 1971, is historically important because it was the first:
practice.solution: Intel 4004 (1971) was the world's first commercially available microprocessor - an entire CPU on one chip - and it launched the 4th generation of computers.

practice.q: Which of the following areas characterises fifth-generation computers?
practice.solution: The 5th generation targets AI, natural-language processing, parallel and quantum-style computing. Punched cards belong to the pre-1st/1st era, assembly is a 2nd-generation language habit, and vacuum tubes are 1st generation.
practice.shortcut: Anything with 'intelligence, learning, robotics, parallel' = 5th generation.

practice.q: PARAM 8000, India's first indigenous supercomputer (1991), was developed by:
practice.solution: PARAM 8000 was built in 1991 by C-DAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing), Pune, under Dr Vijay Bhatkar, after the USA denied Cray supercomputer imports.
practice.shortcut: PARAM always pairs with C-DAC; the denial story (' PARAM = Perform Anvaya Reusable Module') is extra trivia - the developer is what SSC asks.

practice.q: Banks handling lakhs of cheque and transaction records centrally typically deploy:
practice.solution: Mainframes (e.g. IBM zSeries) are built for very high-volume, reliable, simultaneous transaction processing - exactly banking, railways and census workloads.
practice.shortcut: Bulk transactions -> mainframe; raw scientific speed -> supercomputer; one appliance control -> embedded/microcontroller.

practice.q: A device that measures continuous physical quantities like temperature or pressure and outputs a voltage-based result is classified as:
practice.solution: Analog computers work on continuous signals (voltage, speed, temperature) rather than discrete 0/1 digits. Hybrid machines combine analog measurement with digital processing; quantum computers use qubits.
practice.shortcut: 'Continuous quantities' is the keyword for analog; 'counts with digits 0/1' means digital.

practice.q: Which part of the CPU performs subtraction and comparison operations?
practice.solution: Arithmetic (add, subtract) and logical (compare, AND/OR) operations are executed in the ALU. The program counter is a register holding the next instruction's address; the CU only coordinates.
practice.shortcut: Any verb like add/subtract/compare/AND-OR -> ALU, no matter how the question dresses it up.

practice.q: The correct sequence of steps in a single machine cycle is:
practice.solution: The CPU first Fetches the instruction from memory, Decodes it in the control unit, Executes it in the ALU, and Stores the result.
practice.shortcut: Fat Dogs Eat Snacks: Fetch -> Decode -> Execute -> Store. Any option starting with Decode/Execute is out.

practice.q: Assembly language mnemonics such as ADD and MOV are converted into machine code by a(n):
practice.solution: An assembler translates assembly (2GL) mnemonics into machine language. Compilers/interpreters work on high-level (3GL) languages; preprocessors transform source text before compilation.
practice.shortcut: Assembly -> Assembler (same first letters); high-level -> compiler/interpreter.

practice.q: Which of the following is a markup language rather than a programming language?
practice.solution: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) only structures and presents content using tags; it has no logic/control-flow constructs of its own, so it is a markup language. Python, C++ and Java are programming languages.
practice.shortcut: Markup = tags for layout (HTML, XML, Markdown). If the option 'structures web pages', it is not a programming language.

practice.q: Who is known as the first computer programmer for her notes on the Analytical Engine?
practice.solution: Ada Lovelace wrote the first published algorithm intended for Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine, making her the first programmer. Grace Hopper pioneered COBOL and coined 'debugging'.
practice.shortcut: Ada = first program (on paper); Hopper = COBOL + debugging. Don't swap them.

practice.q: The full form of POST, the diagnostic routine that runs when a computer is switched on, is:
practice.solution: POST = Power-On Self-Test: the BIOS/UEFI checks RAM, keyboard, disk controllers etc. before handing over to the boot loader. A failed POST usually beeps.
practice.shortcut: 'Self-Test' is the giveaway - any option without 'Self-Test' is wrong.
